creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A permission dialog that only a person can answer can hold an unattended pane all night. Twice an orchestrator pane (Claude Code in bypass mode, running background subagents) stopped at a subagent's command-approval prompt: 6h40m on 2026-10-12/13 and about 9h30m on 2026-10-24/25. Muster saw it both times and told the agents that had posted to the pane, none of which could answer it. Nothing in the pane's group could have.

Idea (Alex, 2026-10-25): once a pane has sat at such a dialog longer than a threshold, Muster picks the declining choice ("No") and tells the affected agent what it declined and why, so the agent can carry on another way (here, by running the command from a script file). Unlike a_2hIfvs1Cc, which escalates to someone who can answer, this unblocks the pane with nobody present.

Open questions: which dialogs are safe to decline (a command-approval prompt is; a folder-trust dialog or a question the agent put to the person is not); whether to escalate first and decline only after a longer wait; how to recognize a declining choice across harnesses, since today this is Claude Code's prompt and Codex's looks different; and whether it is a per-pane opt-in for unattended runs.
title: Decline a dialog nobody can answer, instead of letting it hold a pane for hours
